work.text: GPU time by the second. A miner, called a provider, runs a small coordinator plus one or more NVIDIA GPU machines and sets an hourly price per machine. What is paid for is a machine that passes the validator's probe: rented machines are paid from one pool, eligible idle machines of the listed models from another.
work.quote: a decentralized GPU rental platform on Bittensor. CLI and Python SDK for renting GPUs, managing pods, and deploying ML workloads

scoring.text: Two formulas. A rented machine scores score x gpu_portion x gpu_count / total count of that model, where gpu_portion is a per-model share the platform derives from rental revenue. An idle machine of an eligible model scores gpu_count x hourly_rate x a cap multiplier, min(idle GPUs in its tier, tier cap) / idle GPUs. Both are multiplied by sysbox, driver and uptime gates.

split.text: Three pools, each proportional inside. Rented machines share the mining pool by score. Idle eligible machines share a second pool sized by their dollar rate per epoch divided by 0.41 and by the epoch's emission in dollars, capped at the burn ceiling. What the idle pool does not claim goes to designated burn UIDs. The packaged ceiling is 0.91, so the rented pool is 0.09.
split.disagrees: The docs emission page says the rented pool is a fixed 13 percent and the ceiling moved from 91 to 87 percent in mid-2026; the live endpoint lium.io/api/v1/shared-config returned total_burn_emission 0.9 on 2026-09-19; the packaged default at the pinned commit is 0.91.

judges.text: Nine validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot, of 64 permitted, though the docs say Lium runs a single validator and point others to a community auditor. Weights are committed then revealed, at most once per 100 blocks. The validator connects to every machine every 15 minutes, checks the sysbox runtime, hardware and a test workload, and reads rental state from the platform's backend.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 9

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The validator checks each machine every 15 minutes, accumulates scores across those cycles, then normalizes and sets weights once per tempo. The idle-pool share is recomputed every cycle from live TAO and alpha prices. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.

buyer.text: Renters paying per GPU-second. The pricing page lists a dollar price per GPU-hour for every model and says every pod is billed per second with no minimum. The docs name developers and AI agents as renters. Providers receive rental fees at the rate the live config sets, 0.95 on 2026-09-19. No customer is named and no dated usage or revenue figure appears on any Lium page.
buyer.quote: billed per second with no minimum

exploits.text: Faked or secretly busy hardware. The validator pins hashes of the NVIDIA management library per driver version, treats a GPU over 95 percent busy with under 1 percent memory as a wedged ghost, and flags held VRAM above 2,048 MB on an idle node. Idle-pool gates: price above market p90 times 1.1, disk under 1.5 times VRAM, no power-cap rights. Without sysbox every score is 0.
